title: Prospect Avenue and plans to gather local musicians for the House That Jazz Built
summary: She wants Bronx musicians like Skeeter Best and Squash to join the House That Jazz Built, located there since 1975.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons

blocks.x: When you lived on Prospect Avenue, what was your address?

1386. I lived there for -- in fact when I leave here I'm going there to see Al Taylor, he just retired from the Parks Department.
What instrument, did he play?
A drummer, he played the drums with Benny Carter, his name is Squash. That's his nickname, Squash. And you know Harold McFarland?
Yeah.
Saxophone player and Al was telling me that Charlie FoWilkes----
You know what I'm trying to do, not getting off the subject --
Al is retired, you know.
Okay. Everybody is, I'm retired, too but I've never been so busy. The House That Jazz Built is in the Bronx and I'm really trying to get something -- the interest started here in the Bronx.
Can I say something?
Because I know that there were a lot of musicians that still live here and I've

been trying to get them together to do the thing because one of the things that bothers me -- it doesn't bother me too much, I realize that everything seems to be shaking downtown, but why can't it shake uptown here, you know? Now, there are little -- I definitely, probably next year to be in a position to promote some of these little concerts in some of these little parks up here because this is where we're coming from.
Can I say something? I'll give you all the assistance I can.
Well, we need to do it.
I'll round them up, I'll get Squash, the drummer. I'll get Skeeter Best.
He lives around here, you say?
Yes, Skeeter Best lives on 730 Soundview Avenue and I'll get the former postmaster, John Strom, who is a very good friend of mine, he blows alto. He used to play with Dizzy Gillespie.
Well, we can get it together because right now I think that The House That Jazz Built is really ready to do some big

Now, you've been located here about five years in the House that Jazz Built, since 1975?
That's right. And you know, it takes time, but we're getting around, a lot of people know about us now.
And I'll get -- I haven't seen him in a couple of months -- Roy Eldridge, when he's in town he'll come up here.
Yeah.
Did you know his brother that blew with Gene?
Sure.
His brother blew a tenor sax.
Did you ever know the Humphrey Brothers?
I heard of them.
They're from Pittsburgh.
I didn't know them.
